author: Sung by the bards of the river holds
pages:
#The Ballad of the Iron Shield

~Old Hakon held the river ford
~with just a shield and spear,
~when forty riders, blades all drawn,
~came thundering to the weir.

~"Stand back, old man," the captain cried,
~"your time of war is done."
~Said Hakon, "Many said the same.
~I'm here. They're dead. Come on."

~He braced his shield of battered iron,
~a hundred battles old;
~each dent a tale, each scar a song,
~each rivet bought with gold.

~They came at him by twos and threes,
~they came at him in ten;
~the river ran with blades and boots
~and the hats of bandit men.

~When dawn came pale across the ford,
~the riders all had fled,
~and Hakon sat upon a stone
~and ate his morning bread.

~So if you cross the river ford,
~go gently, and go slow:
~his shield still hangs above the inn,
~and Hakon? Who can know.
